solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On air row traumatised and exhausted Robert Plant

parts.note: a broadcast that is on air is live

indicators.note: traumatised means shaken up, so the letters of row are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: anagram fodder

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so only the outside letters of Robert remain

parts.note: first and last letters of Robert

explanation.surface: A broadcast quarrel leaves Robert Plant, the Led Zeppelin singer, shaken and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robert Plant' reads as the rock singer, but the surname is the definition. Robert emptied of its insides gives RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A liverwort is a small flowerless green plant related to mosses.

clue.text: Substitute officer upset uniform men at the start

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the officer's abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at the start means only the first letter of men is used

parts.note: first letter of men

explanation.surface: An army officer is annoyed that uniformed men have stood in for him at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: COL (colonel) turned upside down gives LOC, then U and the M that starts men.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who stands in temporarily for another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Sweet eclair Calvin ordered each month

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
ea. is the abbreviation for each
m. is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Someone called Calvin orders an eclair every month as his treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as buying from a shop, which suits the eclair; it is the signal to rearrange. In Britain a sweet is also a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla ice cream is a dessert, and a sweet is the British word for the dessert course.

clue.text: Staggers after receiving shock treatment, puts back in power

indicators.note: the staggers word takes something inside it

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, placed inside REEL…S

explanation.surface: A patient totters about after electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'shock treatment' and 'power' into one medical-electrical picture; 'power' is political, and ECT is the standard abbreviation for electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone back into office.

clue.text: Served up spirit, just missing king … sorry!

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means presented upwards, so the word runs bottom to top
the king falls away, leaving the rest

parts.note: a spook is a ghost; turned upwards it reads KOOPS
KOOPS loses K, the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A waiter who serves the spirits apologises for having just missed the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' next to 'served up' suggests a drink poured; it is a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation of a person owning up to a small blunder, much like sorry.

clue.text: Grotty old vagrant last seen in cave?

definitions.text: Grotty old vagrant last seen in cave?

indicators.note: wandering, so the letters drift out of place
only what is seen last in the next word, its final letter

parts.note: anagram fodder
the last letter of cavE

explanation.surface: A scruffy old tramp was last spotted sheltering in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the wordplay, and it is also a fair picture of a troglodyte.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a cave dweller, and by extension a rough, backward person.

clue.text: Piercing, principally shrill instrument

indicators.note: take the principal, that is the first, letter

parts.note: the first letter of Shrill
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A shrill, piercing instrument, like a whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' and 'shrill' look like two descriptions of the same noise; only 'Piercing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and piercing both describe a point, a pain or a sound.

clue.text: Way to accommodate long bag

indicators.note: the way word finds room inside itself for the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to long for something is to ache for it; placed inside S…T

explanation.surface: A long bag that needs a way of fitting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' sits beside 'bag' like an adjective; it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag of powder or liquid.

clue.text: Cameramen used at broadcast games screened here

indicators.note: scattered widely, as seed is broadcast

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: TV camera crews working at a televised sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameramen, broadcast and screened all belong to television sport; the games are video games shown on arcade machine screens.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is full of video games played on screens.

clue.text: Post Office worker struggling to pen book, one written to raise cash

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen

parts.note: one who toils, labouring hard
b. is the abbreviation for book; it goes inside T…OILER

explanation.surface: A postal worker labours to write a book to make some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing, which suits the surface exactly; here it means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book or artwork churned out simply to earn a living, to keep the pot boiling.

clue.text: Smashing racket crime?

definitions.meaning: the surface pushes an organised scam; the setter means a tennis player hurling a racket down on the court
the question mark flags that this offence is committed against a tennis court, not a court of law

explanation.surface: A tennis player in a tantrum breaks a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests an organised criminal scheme next to 'crime'; it is a tennis racket, and the court is the tennis court rather than the law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is the offence of disrespecting or defying a court of law.

clue.text: Disease from beer we knocked back

indicators.note: knocked backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: WE turned round
mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer

explanation.surface: An illness caught from the beer we drank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking slang for downing a pint, which fits the beer; here it turns WE around.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: mildew is a fungus that attacks plants, one kind of plant disease.

clue.text: Imperative to get little George a close friend

definitions.meaning: the answer, read as a command, is an anagram instruction whose result is GEO, the short form of George

explanation.surface: An urgent need to find a young George a best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: ALTER EGO read as a command says rearrange EGO, and doing so gives GEO, little George. The clue states the result, not the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, hence a trusted, intimate friend.

clue.text: Plucky wife, endlessly zealous officer in reserve

parts.note: game means willing and spirited
w. is the abbreviation for wife
ARDENT without its last letter

explanation.surface: A brave wife is married to an ever-keen army reservist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests reserve soldiers; it is a nature or game reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden polices a game reserve, protecting its wildlife.

clue.text: Huge letters used to spell "Dad", being popular in China

parts.note: giant = huge
Dad is PA, whose letters are P and A: P AND A

explanation.surface: Giant characters spelling out 'Dad' prove popular in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is the noun, a creature, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is China's best-loved animal and national emblem.

clue.text: Young man's backing good quality statesman

parts.note: g = good
a lad's, set behind the G
tone = a quality, as of a sound or voice

explanation.surface: A young man supports a statesman of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts a reversal; here it means supporting from behind, so LAD'S follows G.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was four times British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Knock down chap emitting cry of pain

indicators.note: letting out, so the cry leaves the word

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
ow! is a cry of pain; it comes off the end of the chap word

explanation.surface: A man is knocked down and yells in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap lets out his cry, and FELLOW without OW is FELL; the surface makes emitting sound like shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: felling a tree or a boxer means knocking it to the ground.

clue.text: Deceitful character put up motorway notice

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means raised, so the motorway's name is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a poster is a printed notice put up in public

explanation.surface: Someone has erected a sign beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; its letters MI turned up give IM, then add POSTER for the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is a fraud who pretends to be someone else, a deceiving person.

clue.text: Chief taking off first of the month

indicators.note: removing the opening letter

parts.note: March is a month
MARCH without its first letter M

explanation.surface: The boss takes the first of the month off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The month' is one particular month; the crossing letters show it is March.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy or archbishop.

clue.text: Write uninspiring incomplete ending for literary work

definitions.note: a pentameter is a line of verse, a loose sense of work

parts.note: to pen is to write
tame = dull, uninspiring
TERM, an end, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice to an author to write a dull, unfinished ending for a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending for' reads as the close of the book; ending gives TERM, and 'for' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet, the stuff of literary work.

clue.text: Plastic factory beginning to implement cuts

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the letter goes inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works or factory

indicators.note: beginning to means just the first letter of implement

parts.note: first letter of implement

explanation.surface: A plastics factory is starting to put job cuts into effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic factory' reads as one phrase, but Plastic alone is the definition, as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as an adjective means easily shaped or flexible, just as pliant means bending readily.

clue.text: Italian snail unexpectedly seen around here in France

indicators.note: seen around says the scrambled snail letters are found wrapped round the French word
unexpectedly signals that the letters of snail turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: taken as written: anagram fodder
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: An Italian snail has turned up, surprisingly, in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian snail' reads as one phrase, but Italian is the definition on its own. Crosswords often borrow short French words, as here for 'here in France'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is part of Italy, so a Sicilian is an Italian from that island.

clue.text: Husky is a cracking four-legged friend

indicators.note: the A breaks into the other word

parts.note: a horse, with A inside HO…RSE
the article as printed

explanation.surface: A husky dog is a brilliant four-legged friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog, and 'cracking' like praise; the husky is a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a voice made rough and low by a sore throat.

clue.text: Lament English cricket side, the ultimate in ignominy

parts.note: E = English
the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of ignominY

explanation.surface: Grief over the English cricket team's final disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' reads as a team; in cricket it is also half of the field, leg side and off side.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem or song of mourning, a lament.

clue.text: Congress supporting leaders of White House a tiny bit

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes second
leaders of means the first letter of each of the two words White and House

parts.note: first letters of White and House
it is a coy slang word for sex, and congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: The US Congress backs the President's office only very slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature, but here it means sex, which crosswords render as IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit', so a tiny bit.

clue.text: Inspector isn't overworked by this perfunctory luggage check?

definitions.meaning: a police inspector's easy case, solved at once
a suitcase opened and shut straight away by a customs inspector

explanation.surface: A customs inspector gives the bags a lazy glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The inspector is both a detective and a customs officer, and the case both a crime and a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so clear it is resolved with no effort.

clue.text: This compiler heading west bumped into tourist

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself
to bump into someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: The setter, travelling west, ran into a holidaymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmet is Cornish slang for a tourist, from an old word for ant; heading west to Cornwall is where one meets them.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: Cornish locals call summer visitors emmets, their dialect word for ants.

clue.text: Turned on Conservative about regular instances of vilest infamy

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word on is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards

indicators.note: about says the Conservative surrounds the selected letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

indicators.note: regular instances means every other letter of vilest, taken in order

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of vilest

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician was turned on over repeated cases of the vilest disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' looks like a phrasal verb meaning attacked, but 'Turned' acts on the little word that follows it. 'Regular instances' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, which is what infamy means.
